title: Properness and local quasi-finiteness of a Deligne--Mumford coarse morphism
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $\mathcal X$ be a finite-type Deligne--Mumford stack over $k$ whose diagonal is finite: every scheme base change of its diagonal is a finite scheme morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $q:\mathcal X\to Q$ be a coarse moduli scheme in the convention of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]; thus $Q$ is a $k$-scheme, $q$ is initial for maps to algebraic spaces, and it gives a bijection on isomorphism classes over every algebraically closed field. Then $q$ is proper and locally quasi-finite as a morphism of stacks. There is no linear-reductivity assumption on the geometric stabilizers. Stack, Deligne--Mumford stack, algebraic space and 2-fibre product have the conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids, def-trf-algebraic-space]. For morphisms of these stacks, locally of finite type is tested on smooth scheme charts using [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and finite type additionally requires quasi-compactness. Proper means finite type, universally closed, and having proper relative diagonal. Universally closed means that every base change induces a closed map of underlying point spaces. Locally quasi-finite means locally of finite type, with locally quasi-finite relative diagonal and discrete underlying point space of every field fibre. The point space of a stack consists of its field-valued objects up to isomorphism and common field extension, with the topology detected by a smooth scheme atlas. Properties of representable diagonals are tested on scheme charts; on schemes the proper and locally quasi-finite notions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, pqf-def-quasifinite].

proof.text: For an object $x\in\mathcal X(T)$ over a scheme $T$, the pullback of the inertia projection to $T$ is the automorphism sheaf $\operatorname{Isom}_T(x,x)$. This is exactly the scheme base change of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ by the pair $(x,x):T\to\mathcal X\times_k\mathcal X$: the 2-fibre product description of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] has as its objects an isomorphism between the two copies of $x$. The finite-diagonal hypothesis therefore says directly that this is a finite $T$-scheme [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. This checks finiteness of the inertia projection on every scheme test, with no hypothesis about stabilizer reductivity.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, theorem-keel-mori, and definition-categorical-quotient; agent-written DM consequence

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-keel-mori-finite-inertia-quotient] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the inertia finiteness just checked. It gives an algebraic space $M/k$ and a categorical map $p:\mathcal X\to M$ which is separated, quasi-compact and a universal homeomorphism. In particular the relative diagonal of $p$ is proper. The theorem requires finite inertia, not a tame or linearly reductive stabilizer.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, theorem-keel-mori, and definition-categorical-quotient; agent-written DM consequence

proof.text: The coarse initial property in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] gives a unique $k$-map $a:Q\to M$ with $aq=p$; the categorical property in [lem-sfb-keel-mori-finite-inertia-quotient] gives a unique $k$-map $b:M\to Q$ with $bp=q$. Now $(ba)q=q$ and $(ab)p=p$. The same two uniqueness properties imply $ba=1_Q$ and $ab=1_M$. Thus $a$ is an isomorphism identifying $q$ with $p$. Under this isomorphism every base-change diagram, relative diagonal, and underlying point space for $q$ is the corresponding one for $p$. Hence $q$ has proper relative diagonal, is quasi-compact, and is a universal homeomorphism. The argument uses only initiality of the assumed coarse map, so needs no claim that arbitrary base change preserves a coarse moduli universal property.

source.place: Tag 0DUT, theorem-keel-mori, and definition-categorical-quotient; agent-written DM consequence

proof.text: Choose a smooth scheme atlas $u:U\to\mathcal X$ in the chart definition of local finite type for $\mathcal X/k$. Thus $U\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is locally of finite type. Apply clause (a) of [lemma-nagata-finite-type-to-separated-target] to the scheme maps $qu:U\to Q$ and $Q\to\operatorname{Spec}k$: their composite is the structure map of $U$, so $qu$ is locally of finite type. By the chart convention in the item this is precisely local finite type of $q$, with the identity chart on the scheme $Q$. Together with quasi-compactness from step 3 it gives finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and the stack convention in the statement. Clause (b), which requires a separated second arrow, is not used: $Q/k$ need not be assumed separated.

source.place: Tag 06U9, lemma-finite-type-permanence, specialized to scheme target and base; its chart proof uses scheme cancellation Tag 01T8

proof.text: After every base change $\mathcal Z\to Q$, step 3 gives a homeomorphism $|\mathcal X\times_Q\mathcal Z|\to|\mathcal Z|$. A homeomorphism sends closed sets to closed sets, so $q$ is universally closed. Step 4 gives finite type and step 3 gives a proper relative diagonal. These are exactly the three conditions defining properness in the item, so $q$ is proper.

To test the relative diagonal $\Delta_q$ on a scheme $T\to\mathcal X\times_Q\mathcal X$, write its datum as objects $x,y\in\mathcal X(T)$ with equal images in $Q(T)$. Because $Q$ is a sheaf of sets regarded as a discrete groupoid, every isomorphism $x\to y$ automatically induces the unique identity between these equal images. Thus the pullback of $\Delta_q$ is exactly $\operatorname{Isom}_T(x,y)$, also the pullback of $\Delta_{\mathcal X/k}$ by $(x,y)$. It is a finite scheme over $T$ by hypothesis. By [pqf-lem-finite-qf] it is quasi-finite, and by the forward implication of [pqf-lem-qf-locqf-qc] it is therefore locally quasi-finite in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite]. This proves local quasi-finiteness of $\Delta_q$ on all scheme tests; the identification is the explicit 2-fibre product calculation of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids].

source.place: Tag 06PU, definition-locally-quasi-finite; direct calculation of the relative diagonal; finite scheme morphisms are quasi-finite

proof.text: For every field $K$ and every $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Q$, the universal-homeomorphism assertion of step 3 gives $|\mathcal X\times_Q\operatorname{Spec}K|\simeq|\operatorname{Spec}K|$. The latter is a one-point space and is discrete. Thus all field fibres have discrete underlying point spaces, including for non-algebraically closed $K$. Combining this with local finite type from step 4 and local quasi-finiteness of the relative diagonal from step 6 gives exactly local quasi-finiteness of $q$ as defined in the statement. If $\mathcal X$ is empty, the categorical uniqueness argument gives $Q$ empty, and the field-fibre condition is vacuous.
